claims.claim_text: The indexed Manuel Segal is a high-confidence match to the National Broadcasting sound-effects engineer later documented on the OSS Soldatensender staff.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official Army record agrees by exact name and nonshared protected identifier; contemporary and scholarly sources independently preserve the same uncommon name and sound-effects specialty before and during OSS service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from exact-name protected-identifier agreement plus an occupation-specific NBC-to-OSS bridge.
claims.temporal_assessment: National Broadcasting employment is documented in May 1943, before Army entry in August 1943 and later OSS Soldatensender work.
claims.match_notes: No Army coded occupation value is used. The employer finding rests on the contemporary radio-industry source and the independently documented OSS specialty.

claims.claim_text: National Broadcasting Company is the best-supported last civilian employer before Manuel Segal's wartime Army and OSS service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A May 1943 radio-industry article places Segal among National Broadcasting sound engineers; Army evidence dates entry later that year, and Soley documents the same specialty on the OSS Soldatensender staff.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity match from the official protected-identifier crosswalk and occupation-specific chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded rather than explicit: no later civilian employer is documented between May 1943 NBC work and August 1943 Army entry.
claims.match_notes: NBC is not labeled the immediate pre-OSS affiliation because the reviewed evidence includes intervening Army service but does not name the Army-to-OSS unit path.
